 21 IPS Trainees Complete Kashmir Counter-Terrorism Field Module with CRPF
 November 8, 2026 
 0 Comments
 Share
 Share
 Link 
 Close share 
 Copy link 
 A five-day familiarization programme in Kashmir for 21 Indian Police Service (IPS) officer trainees from the 78th Regular Recruit (RR) Batch, Second Batch, concluded on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The module gave the future police officers practical exposure to counter-terrorism operations, security-force procedures and the challenges of working in the Kashmir Valley.
 Designed to connect classroom learning with field experience, the programme introduced the trainees to the region’s security environment and the operational responsibilities of forces deployed there. The trainees were divided into small groups and attached to different companies of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), allowing them to observe operational practices and learn about the demands of counter-terrorism and internal security duties.
 During their attachments, they were exposed to Cordon and Search Operations (CASO), the functioning of Tactical Operation Bases (TOBs) and routine operational activities. The trainees also learned about the administrative, tactical and operational frameworks used by security forces in high-intensity security environments.
 The programme’s final day included tactical briefings and demonstrations focused on modern counter-terrorism operations. A live room intervention demonstration showed the trainees procedures used in close-quarter security operations.
 The officer trainees also visited the War Room, Social Media Cell and Madadgaar Cell. These visits introduced them to operational coordination, information monitoring and public assistance mechanisms. A display of specialized weapons and modern operational equipment provided a further look at the resources used by security personnel in demanding operational conditions.
 The module ended with an interactive feedback and debriefing session. Trainees shared observations, discussed operational lessons and reflected on what they had experienced during their field attachments.
 The field-based training gave the 21 IPS officer trainees a closer understanding of counter-terrorism work, coordination among agencies and the responsibilities involved in leading in sensitive security settings. The practical exposure is intended to support their professional preparation for future leadership roles in law enforcement and internal security across the country.
